evidence.note: Before writing code, reads run_tests.sh/py, filter.json, expected_results.json and many individual test .c files to understand the pass/fail signal and required features — establishing what verification will measure.

Adds a -S flag specifically to emit assembly, then reads generated asm for failing test 00100.c to localize concrete codegen bugs (double epilogue, reversed subtraction, _start conflict) rather than assuming correctness.

Compiles single failing test 00004.c to assembly, spots 'movl (%rax), %rax' width mismatch, reasons about what correct output should be (%eax), and fixes the specific load path — root-cause isolation to the codegen pass.
Runs batch loops over targeted test-ID subsets (e.g. 00083-00088) and distinguishes defect categories (function-like macros = preprocessor, variadic = parser, asm syntax = codegen) to guide fixes.

Tracks per-suite pass breakdown (c_testsuite 79/146, wacc 135/221, gcc_torture 63/413) from existing runner output to prioritize the most tractable failures — but relies on the handed-over runner, with no regression guards (score oscillated 262→294→277).

reasoning: The agent consistently goes beyond the level-5 pattern: it doesn't just run subsets and read pass/fail, it reduces to individual failing tests, adds an assembly-dump flag, inspects generated asm, and reasons about what correct output should look like to pinpoint the buggy pass (lexer/parser/sema/codegen) — clear level-8 behaviors sustained across the whole trajectory. It falls short of a full 8/10 because it uses whole existing test files as repros rather than crafting minimal cases, never diffs against a known-correct reference (gcc -S), and builds no verification infrastructure or regression guards beyond the handed-over runner, despite visible score regressions. This places it solidly at 7.
